subject: maths
title: Time: the 12-Hour and 24-Hour Clock
seo_title: Year 4 12- and 24-Hour Clock Worksheets: Analogue, Digital and Converting Time (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Read, write and convert time between analogue and digital 12- and 24-hour clocks; solve problems involving converting from hours to minutes; minutes to seconds; years to months; weeks to days.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on time: read analogue clocks to the minute, write am and pm times, convert between the 12-hour and 24-hour clock, work out durations, read bus and train timetables and convert hours, minutes, seconds, weeks and years. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: pm: add 12 to the hour. 3:45 pm = 15:45.
key_sub: am times keep the hour with 4 digits (7:30 am = 07:30). Midnight is 00:00. An hour has 60 minutes, so count on to the next o’clock when you work out how long.
body_html:
Analogue clocks: past and to

The hour hand is short. The minute hand is long. When the minute hand is on the right-hand side, say minutes past the hour. When it is on the left-hand side, say minutes to the next hour.

TimeWe say
7:15quarter past 7
7:2020 past 7
7:30half past 7
7:3525 to 8
7:45quarter to 8
7:528 minutes to 8

12-hour time: am and pm

A day has 24 hours, but a clock face only shows 12. So we write am for times from midnight to noon (night and morning) and pm for times from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

Analogue to digital

The clock shows 20 to 4 in the afternoon. Write it as a 12-hour time.

20 to 4 is 40 minutes past 3. It is the afternoon, so it is pm.

Answer: 3:40 pm

24-hour time

The 24-hour clock counts the hours from 00 to 23, so you do not need am or pm. It always has 4 digits: 07:30, 15:45. Bus and train timetables use it.

12-hour24-hourRule
7:30 am07:30am: keep the hour, write 4 digits
12:00 noon12:0012 pm: keep 12
3:45 pm15:45pm: add 12 (3 + 12 = 15)
9:10 pm21:10pm: add 12 (9 + 12 = 21)
12:20 am00:20just after midnight: 00

To go back from 24-hour to 12-hour time, take away 12 from hours 13 to 23: 18:05 is 6:05 pm.

How long? Count on in jumps

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers. Jump to the next o’clock first, then to the end time.

Read a timetable

A bus leaves the Bus Station at 15:40 and gets to Park Road at 16:18. How long is the journey?

15:40 to 16:00 is 20 minutes. 16:00 to 16:18 is 18 minutes. 20 + 18 = 38.

Answer: 38 minutes

Converting units of time

Bigger unitSmaller unit
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days
1 year12 months

Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. For mixed units, add the extra part.

Hours to minutes

2 hours 15 minutes = ? minutes

2 × 60 = 120. 120 + 15 = 135.

Answer: 135 minutes

Days to weeks

23 days = ? weeks and days

3 × 7 = 21. 23 − 21 = 2.

Answer: 3 weeks 2 days

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3:45 pm written as 13:45 or 03:45pm: add 12 to the hour. 3 + 12 = 15, so 15:45
15:45 read as 5:45 pmTake away 12, do not just drop the 1. 15 − 12 = 3, so 3:45 pm
12:20 am written as 12:20Just after midnight is 00 in 24-hour time: 00:20
Minute hand on 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes
Quarter to 4 written as 4:45Quarter to 4 is 15 minutes before 4:00, so 3:45
14:35 to 15:10 worked out as 1510 − 1435 = 75 minutesAn hour is 60 minutes. Count on: 25 + 10 = 35 minutes

faq.q: When do children learn the 24-hour clock?
faq.a: In the National Curriculum in England, children learn to read, write and convert between analogue and digital 12- and 24-hour clocks in Year 4. In Year 3 they tell the time to the nearest minute and use am and pm.

faq.q: How do you change 12-hour time into 24-hour time?
faq.a: For am times keep the hour and write 4 digits (7:30 am is 07:30). For pm times add 12 to the hour (3:45 pm is 15:45). 12 noon stays 12:00 and 12 midnight is 00:00.
In 24-hour time midnight is written 00:00, the start of a new day. So 12:20 am is 00:20 and noon is 12:00.

faq.q: What time conversions should a Year 4 child know?
faq.a: Year 4 children should convert hours to minutes, minutes to seconds, years to months and weeks to days, using 1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 year = 12 months and 1 week = 7 days.

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. In the evening means pm, so it is 7:20 pm.

items.q: Write 10 past 9 at night as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 past 9” means 10 minutes after 9 o’clock: 9:10. At night means pm, so it is 9:10 pm.

items.q: Write quarter to 9 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 9” means 15 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 8:45. In the morning means am, so it is 8:45 am.

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 3:35. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 3:35 pm.

items.q: Write 10 to 12 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 to 12” means 10 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 11:50. In the morning means am, so it is 11:50 am.

items.q: Write 5 to 5 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “5 to 5” means 5 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 4:55. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 4:55 pm.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is quarter to 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: “quarter to 4” is 15 minutes before 4 o’clock: 3:45 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 15:45.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is 25 to 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: “25 to 4” is 25 minutes before 4 o’clock: 3:35 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 15:35.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is 20 past 9 in the evening?
items.e: “20 past 9” is 9:20 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So it is 21:20.

The hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The minute hand is 2 small marks past the 5. Count in 5s to the 5 (25), then on in 1s: 27 minutes past. It is 9:27 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So it is 21:27.

items.q: How many minutes are in 4 hours?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.

items.q: How many seconds are in 5 minutes?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 5 × 60 = 300 seconds.

items.q: How many months are in 4 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. 4 × 12 = 48 months.

items.q: How many days are in 6 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days.
2 × 60 = 120 minutes. Then add the 20 minutes: 120 + 20 = 140 minutes.
4 × 60 = 240 seconds. Then add the 50 seconds: 240 + 50 = 290 seconds.
60 minutes make 1 hour. 170 = 60 + 60 + 50, so 170 minutes = 2 hours 50 minutes.
60 seconds make 1 minute. 2 × 60 = 120, and 130 − 120 = 10. So 130 seconds = 2 minutes 10 seconds.
12 months make 1 year. 4 × 12 = 48, and 51 − 48 = 3. So 51 months = 4 years 3 months. (Do not split by 10: a year has 12 months.)
7 days make 1 week. 3 × 7 = 21, and 23 − 21 = 2. So 23 days = 3 weeks 2 days.

items.q: How long is it from 08:05 to 08:30?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 30 − 5 = 25 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 11:25 to 11:40?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 40 − 25 = 15 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 16:25 to 16:40?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 40 − 25 = 15 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 13:50 to 14:05?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 13:50 to 14:00 is 10 minutes. Then 14:00 to 14:05 is 5 minutes. 10 + 5 = 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 09:45 to 10:15?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 09:45 to 10:00 is 15 minutes. Then 10:00 to 10:15 is 15 minutes. 15 + 15 = 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 17:56 to 18:13?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 17:56 to 18:00 is 4 minutes. Then 18:00 to 18:13 is 13 minutes. 4 + 13 = 17 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 16:36 to 17:15?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 16:36 to 17:00 is 24 minutes. Then 17:00 to 17:15 is 15 minutes. 24 + 15 = 39 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 14:15 to 15:35?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 14:15 to 15:00 is 45 minutes. Then 15:00 to 15:35 is 35 minutes. 45 + 35 = 80 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 16:50 to 17:55?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 16:50 to 17:00 is 10 minutes. Then 17:00 to 17:55 is 55 minutes. 10 + 55 = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 15:10 to 16:25?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 15:10 to 16:00 is 50 minutes. Then 16:00 to 16:25 is 25 minutes. 50 + 25 = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: The bus leaves the Bus Station at 16:30. What time does it get to Park Road?
items.e: Find 16:30 in the Bus Station row. Go down that column to the Park Road row: 17:11.

items.q: A bus gets to the Library at 17:25. What time did it leave the Bus Station?
items.e: Find 17:25 in the Library row. Go up that column to the Bus Station row: 17:00.

items.q: How long does the bus that leaves the Bus Station at 16:30 take to get to Park Road?
items.e: 16:30 to 17:00 is 30 minutes. 17:00 to 17:11 is 11 minutes. 30 + 11 = 41 minutes.

items.q: Kai must be at Park Road by 16:50. What is the latest bus he can catch from Market Square?
items.e: Look along the Park Road row for the last time that is not after 16:50: 16:41. Go up that column to Market Square: 16:12. The next bus gets to Park Road at 17:11, which is too late.

items.q: Lily gets to Market Square at 16:48, just after a bus has left. How long must she wait for the next one?
items.e: The bus at 16:42 has gone. The next bus from Market Square is at 17:12. From 16:48 to 17:12 is 24 minutes.

items.q: Harry’s bus gets to the Library at 3:55 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 3:55 pm is in the afternoon or evening, so add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. Look for 15:55 in the Library row.

items.q: Tea is at 17:30. A pie takes 45 minutes to cook. What time must it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 30 minutes to 17:00. Then count back 15 more minutes: 16:45.

items.q: A film starts at 18:50 and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: 18:50 + 1 hour = 19:50. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes to 20:00, then 25 more minutes: 20:25.

items.q: Arjun’s holiday lasts 3 weeks 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days.

items.q: Jack is 8 years 7 months old. How old is he in months?
items.e: 8 years = 8 × 12 = 96 months. 96 + 7 = 103 months.

items.q: The train leaves Oakfield at 07:55. What time does it get to City Centre?
items.e: Find 07:55 in the Oakfield row. Go down that column to the City Centre row: 08:36.

items.q: A train gets to Hillside at 08:58. What time did it leave Oakfield?
items.e: Find 08:58 in the Hillside row. Go up that column to the Oakfield row: 08:35.

items.q: How long does the train that leaves Oakfield at 07:55 take to get to City Centre?
items.e: 07:55 to 08:00 is 5 minutes. 08:00 to 08:36 is 36 minutes. 5 + 36 = 41 minutes.

items.q: Grace must be at City Centre by 09:05. What is the latest train she can catch from Bridgeton?
items.e: Look along the City Centre row for the last time that is not after 09:05: 08:56. Go up that column to Bridgeton: 08:24. The next train gets to City Centre at 09:16, which is too late.

items.q: Oliver gets to Bridgeton at 07:52, just after a train has left. How long must he wait for the next one?
items.e: The train at 07:44 has gone. The next train from Bridgeton is at 08:04. From 07:52 to 08:04 is 12 minutes.

items.q: Evie’s train gets to Hillside at 8:38 am. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 8:38 am is in the morning, so the hour stays the same. Write it with 4 digits: 08:38.

items.q: Alfie goes to bed at 19:30. He reads for 25 minutes before bed. What time does he start reading?
items.e: Count back 25 minutes from 19:30: 19:30 − 25 minutes = 19:05.

items.q: A song lasts 3 minutes 40 seconds. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 3 minutes = 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. 180 + 40 = 220 seconds.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 am and finishes at 3:15 pm. How long is the school day?
items.e: 8:45 am to 2:45 pm is 6 hours. 2:45 pm to 3:15 pm is 30 minutes. 6 hours + 30 minutes = 6 hours 30 minutes.

items.q: Noah has a 45-minute swimming lesson every week. How long does he swim in 4 weeks?
items.e: 4 × 45 = 180 minutes. 60 minutes make 1 hour, so 180 minutes = 3 × 60 = 3 hours.
